title: sccap session metadata
description: Metadata sidecar for a capture bundle. Superset of docs/Star-Conflict-Capture-Protocol.md 2.4. A bundle with only pcapng segments and a valid instance of this document is a valid session.

schema_version.description: Bundle schema version. Readers MUST refuse an unknown MAJOR with an explicit diagnostic (FR-027).

protocol_tables_version.description: Revision of the embedded protocol element tables (docs/protocol/) this build used, so a coverage claim can be traced to the table revision that produced it.

protocol_lib_commit.description: DEPRECATED, schema 1.0 only. Pinned the external starconflict protocol library, before Principle VI was amended on 2026-08-13 to require a single in-repo implementation. Readers MUST still accept it on existing bundles.

utc_end.description: Absent or null for an interrupted session. Absence does not invalidate the bundle.

anchors.description: Paired realtime/monotonic readings. Makes monotonic time recoverable for any pcapng frame and makes a wall-clock step visible rather than corrupting (FR-003).

mode.description: passive is the default; relay means an interposition overlay was active (Principle IV).

rewrites.description: Every rewrite performed, enumerated. MUST be empty when mode is passive (FR-010).

client.description: Identity of the game build this session was captured against, detected automatically from the platform's application manifest and the client executable. A recording without its matching client build is frequently undecodable, so this is what lets a reader years later confirm they hold the same executable that produced these bytes. Absent when no install could be found; the session records an anomaly saying so.

build_id.description: Platform build id (e.g. Steam buildid). Identifies the release, but may be reused; binary_sha256 is the unambiguous identity.

depot_manifests.description: Depot id to content manifest id. Pins the exact installed content, and unlike an owner id refers to content rather than a person.

install_path.description: Install location with the user's home directory replaced by '~'. Which library the game sits in is worth recording; the account name on the machine is not, and sessions get shared.

binary_sha256.description: Hash of the client executable. The strongest build identity available: a build id can be reused, a hash cannot.

binary_build_id.description: GNU build-id from the executable's ELF notes — the compiler's own stamp on this exact binary.

runtime.description: e.g. 'native' or a Wine/Proton build. Changes what a reader should expect of the capture, notably how TLS key material could have been obtained.

source.description: How the client was identified, so a reader can weigh an autodetected install against a hand-supplied path.

capture_filter.description: Empty by default. A non-empty value is a capture-time discard decision and MUST be warned about (Principle I).

snaplen.description: 0 means full frame, the default. Any other value is a capture-time truncation and MUST be warned about.

packets_dropped.description: Kernel drop counter. Must be 0 for the session to pass verification without warning (SC-002).

sensitive.description: Always true. Every session is sensitive by default (FR-031).

credential_warning.description: Set when CCMD_AUTH_REQUEST or AC_PLAYER_CREDENTIALS traffic was observed (FR-033).

economy_ledger.description: Optional contributor-supplied before/after currency integers. Converts blind structural analysis of payload into a grep (manual 2.4).
